profile.reading: This TierPoint facility is located in Saint Louis, Missouri, TierPoint's own corporate headquarters market, where the company operates three separate named data centers rather than one. Millpark, at 2315 Millpark Drive in suburban Maryland Heights, is the smallest of the three at more than 23,000 total square feet. Olive, at 1111 Olive Street in downtown St. Louis, spans more than 124,000 total square feet with an N+1 power design and 10-gigabit wave interconnection to other regional TierPoint sites. Locust, at 2300 Locust Street also in downtown St. Louis, is the newest and most significant of the three: TierPoint acquired the building outright on August 13, 2024, with a planned total investment of up to 150 million dollars, and CEO Jerry Kent described it as a direct response to strong demand for data center and AI-GPU workload capacity, with the completed facility expected to become TierPoint's second-largest data center company-wide by critical load capacity, supporting roughly 80 construction jobs and 9 permanent positions. Because this single map record could not be confidently matched to one of the three specific St. Louis facilities this session, all three are documented here honestly rather than guessing at which one the record represents. All three carry TierPoint's standard SOC 1 and SOC 2 Type II (including HITRUST), HIPAA, PCI-DSS, GLBA, and ISO 27001 compliance package. TierPoint, headquartered in St. Louis, was formed in 2010 and now operates roughly 40 data centers across 20 US markets. As is standard industry practice, tenant identities are not publicly disclosed.

reading.body:
TierPoint operates three distinct facilities in the Saint Louis area, its own corporate headquarters market: Millpark at over 23,000 square feet in suburban Maryland Heights, Olive at over 124,000 square feet in downtown Saint Louis with N+1 power design and regional fiber interconnection, and Locust at over 135,800 square feet also downtown, acquired outright in August 2024 as part of a planned total investment up to $150 million. The company's CEO stated Locust will become TierPoint's second-largest data center by critical load capacity upon completion and described the acquisition as a direct response to demand for AI-GPU workload capacity. This single map record cannot be confidently matched to one of the three facilities.

No megawatt figures are published for any of the three Saint Louis facilities or for any other data center in Missouri in this site's current research, so the scale of IT load these buildings will support cannot be quantified from operator specifications. The Locust acquisition's magnitude and CEO framing suggest material significance to regional AI infrastructure, but capacity remains unstated.

All three facilities carry SOC 1 and SOC 2 Type II (including HITRUST), HIPAA, PCI-DSS, GLBA, and ISO 27001 certifications, qualifying them for regulated healthcare, financial, and enterprise workloads. TierPoint operates approximately 40 data centers across 20 US markets, making these Saint Louis facilities part of a larger regional footprint but not isolated assets. Missouri has eight mapped data center facilities total, none with published megawatt capacity, so these three represent the state's only named critical load figures available to this site, which are zero.
